problem: When the user said a named person 'replied', retrieval surfaced multiple conversations with that person and semantic/topical similarity overrode the actual chronological reply relationship.
required_behavior: For phrases such as 'X replied', 'X answered', 'they said back', or equivalent, resolve the referent first against the most recent actual outbound message/question to that named person in the available conversation/history.
Chronological conversational adjacency and explicit recipient identity outrank topical or lexical similarity.
Use semantic/topic matching only when no chronological antecedent can be recovered.
If multiple chronological antecedents remain genuinely plausible, inspect the relevant recent history before interpreting the reply; do not silently select a thematically similar older thread.
A reply's wording may overlap an unrelated topic and must not override an established response edge.
regression: If Louka's current reply mentions that something 'worked', crying, or 'energy awakening', but the most recent message sent to Louka concerned a loving-adult/inner-child exercise, bind the reply to that message unless the reply explicitly names another antecedent. Do not redirect it to an older shaking/Qigong thread based only on topical overlap.
scope: Universal conversational retrieval/referent resolution; does not replace explicit user corrections or exact quoted reply context.
